cta_mid_title: Want to know exactly where your money is leaking?
tech_sub: We work best with companies where the work is done by people on-site, not in an office — one crew or several, it doesn't matter: tracking runs on Excel, WhatsApp and the owner's memory, and there are already too many sites to hold in your head.
tech_sub_mobile: Companies where the work happens on-site and tracking runs on Excel and the owner's memory.
ideal_note: We also work with warehouses, logistics and small manufacturing — different tasks, same approach.
faq_a1: The system doesn't make money on its own — it shows you where you're losing it: rates below average, unbilled extra work, missing receipts. The payback maths is simple: what one missed piece of extra work or one underpriced rate costs you, and how many of those you have a month. Call us — we'll run the numbers on your sites, not in general.
faq_a2: The price depends on the task and is named before work starts. Objecty — a launch, then a subscription based on the number of crews. We'll give the exact figure by phone.
faq_q3: Do we need to have systems or vendors already selected?
faq_a3: No. We can start from scratch — picking the right tools, improving what you've got, or just working out where to begin. We're not tied to any vendor, so the advice is about what fits your situation.
faq_q4: Can it connect to our existing systems?
faq_a4: Yes. Most often that is the task itself — connecting what already works instead of starting from scratch.
faq_q6: What if there is nothing to automate?
faq_a6: Then we'll say so. If a process change or a spreadsheet template is enough, that's what you'll hear from us.
faq_q7: What kinds of companies do you work with?
faq_a7: Small and mid-sized businesses with a lot of manual work. We know best the companies where the work happens on-site — construction, renovation, installation, service.
faq_a8: We do. Support is part of the subscription: server, updates, replies during working hours.
faq_a9: The data is yours — export it any time. The technology is ordinary, so any developer can maintain the system. The source code can be handed over by contract if needed.
